title: RBAC v2 compatibility matrix and forensics export
content:
Summary:
This tactical guide defines a compatibility matrix for RBAC v2 clients, plus the canonical "forensics" SIEM export format and the pragmatic rollout strategy to deploy evidence automation with minimal customer disruption. The focus: make forensic telemetry useful for incident analysis (complete, normalized, tamper-evident), keep a safe migration from RBAC v1, and provide automated transforms for downstream SIEMs without requiring consumers to understand internal entitlement model changes.

Goals:
- Define a stable export schema optimized for root-cause and post-incident timelines (event-level, context, derived entitlements).
- Provide a compatibility matrix for API clients, agents, and 3rd-party connectors so teams can validate expectations during rollout.
- Prescribe a phased deployment plan with canaries, sampling rules, and fallbacks.
- Supply a QA checklist and verification queries for SRE/CS/Legal.

Scope:
- Covers RBAC v2 server-side responsibility for producing evidence and the expected shape consumed by SIEM/forensics pipelines.
- Not prescriptive about long-term archival retention policy (handled by Governance), but includes recommended retention buckets for incident work.
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; where customer-managed SIEMs exist we provide transformation hooks and export contract definitions.

Compatibility matrix (high level):
- Matrix rows: client type / SDK / internal service / external connector. Columns: RBAC v1 support, RBAC v2 coarse entitlements, V2 attribute qualifiers supported, transform needed, recommended rollout action.
- Example entries (line format: client | v1 | v2-basic | v2-attrs | transform | action):
  - api-sdk-js | yes | yes | partial | server-side enrich | canary on 5% traffic
  - console-web | yes | yes | full | client shim (thin) | staged release across regions
  - infra-agent | yes | no | N/A | mandatory agent update | coordinated upgrade window
  - sqs-ingest | yes | yes | partial | mapping table | enable dual-write for 2 weeks

Compatibility notes and risk levels:
- Low-risk: clients that only need coarse allow/deny semantics. No changes required; server emits v1-compatible summary fields.
- Medium-risk: clients that use entitlement names as identifiers. These require rename mappings and a short deprecation alias period.
- High-risk: agents that embed entitlement structure in downstream data models (e.g., analytics pipelines). These require explicit migration windows, transform jobs, and QA.

Forensics export schema (canonical):
- Top-level contract: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) events, each event is a single audit action. Schema must be stable and backwards-compatible across minor versions.
- Recommended exporter behavior: emit both "canonical" fields and a compact "raw" payload for full context. Consumers should default to canonical fields.

Canonical event fields (field: type - description):
- event_id: string - cryptographic UUID for traceability (v4 + signing should be supported).
- timestamp_utc: string (ISO8601) - event emission time (server time).
- recorded_at: string (ISO8601) - when event was persisted to the export sink (helps ingestion ordering).
- actor: string - principal id (user:<id> | service:<id>), normalized.
- actor_ip: string - best-effort client IP address.
- action: string - high-level action verb (e.g., token.create, resource.read, permission.eval).
- resource: string - resource canonical id (resource-type/resource-id).
- resource_attrs: string[] - list of key=value pairs for resource context (optional).
- decision: string - allow | deny | conditional | unknown.
- decision_reason: string - shortened canonical reason code (e.g., "entitlement-missing", "rate-limited", "fallback-to-global").
- entitlement_paths: string[] - list of entitlement path strings evaluated for this action in order of evaluation (new in v2).
- matched_rule: string - id of policy/rule that produced the decision.
- resolved_attributes: string[] - attribute qualifiers that affected decision (e.g., {region=eu, env=prod}).
- model_version: string - RBAC engine artifact SHA or semver.
- provenance: string - origin tag (hosted, dedicated:<pool>, private:<customer-id>).
- signature: string - optional base64 signature of the event body (for tamper evidence).
- raw_payload: string - compressed and base64 encoded raw decision trace (optional but recommended for forensics).

Notes on fields:
- entitlement_paths is a first-class field in v2: it provides the ordered list of entitlements consulted. This avoids requiring downstream teams to query the policy service for historical context during an investigation.
- signature is optional for on-prem exports where HSM/KMS may be unavailable; hosted exports should sign by default.

SIEM mapping guidance (transform layer):
- Provide a reference transform lib (Go/Node/Python) that ingests the canonical NDJSON and emits the SIEM-specific fields. Keep transforms minimal: map event_id->event_id, timestamp_utc->@timestamp, actor->user.name, decision->event.outcome, matched_rule->rule.id, entitlement_paths->labels.entitlements.
- Normalize decision_reason into a 3-token taxonomy so SIEM filters can be terse (e.g., "deny:entitlement", "allow:policy-exception").
- For Splunk/Elastic: include raw_payload as a compressed artifact and expand to separate indices only when customers request deeper indexing.

Forensics export performance & size expectations:
- Typical event size (canonical fields only): 0.8-1.4 KB. With raw_payload average 6-12 KB.
- Throughput: exporters must support bursty spikes up to 2500 eps per tenant for large customers.
- Backpressure strategy: when export sinks are slow, buffer to local durable queue (rocksdb-backed), apply sampling policy, and expose the queue length metric with alert thresholds.

Transformation / aliasing rules for migration:
- Provide a server-side alias table that maps v1 entitlement names to the new v2 entitlement_paths for a grace window. Map must be editable via governance UI and exported with the forensics payload as "migration_aliases": ["v1:old-entitlement->v2:path/alpha"].
- All aliasing is logged; any alias used for a decision appends a synthetic audit event with event_type="alias-used" and references the original event_id.

Export pipeline options:
- Streaming (preferred): push to SIEM via HTTPS or syslog; events are sent as they happen. Use producer acknowledgements and a short-lived retry queue.
- Batch (fall-back): periodic bulk export (1-5 min windows). Include window_start/window_end and upto N events per file. Bulk exports must carry manifest.json with counts and SHA256 checksums.
- Dual-write: during migration, emit both old v1-compatible export and v2 canonical export. Dual-write flagged with header "x-export-mode: dual".

Sampling & retention recommendations:
- For initial rollout: 100% capture for decisions that result in deny/conditional, 10% sample for allow. After stable, reduce allow sampling to 1% for high-volume tenants.
- Retention buckets (recommended):
  - hot (30 days) for full raw_payload and signatures
  - warm (180 days) for canonical fields only
  - cold (>= 365 days) for summarized records (no raw_payload)

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 — Preparation (2 weeks):
  - Finalize canonical schema and publish transform libs.
  - Create compatibility test harness and dataset that simulates 6 common tenant profiles.
  - Update docs and run internal training for CS and SRE.

Phase 1 — Internal canary (1 week):
  - Enable v2 export in internal accounts only.
  - Validate ingestion to internal SIEM, run 5 pre-defined incident playbooks.
  - Run automated integrity checks (event signing, checksum validation).

Phase 2 — External canary (2-4 weeks):
  - Identify 3 low-volume customers across regions who opt in.
  - Dual-write: both legacy export and v2 canonical.
  - Monitor drift metrics: decision parity, entitlement path differences, event size, latency.
  - Success criteria: decision parity >= 99.8% for allow/deny in scope, export latency < 1s p95.

Phase 3 — Gradual roll (6-8 weeks):
  - Ramp to 20% of tenants, then 50%, then 100% over scheduled windows.
  - Offer migration assistance for medium/high risk tenants (mapping workshops, transform scripts).

Phase 4 — Deprecation of v1 artifacts (8–12 weeks post full roll):
  - Announce deprecation windows to customers with a 12-week notice.
  - Keep aliasing legacy names for additional 12 weeks in export, then stop.

Operational runbooks & QA checklist (for SRE and CS):
- Runbook snippets:
  - If SIEM ingestion falls below expected EPS: Bump buffer retention, enable batch export, notify on-call.
  - If parity drops: roll back to dual-write and run a diff job across the last 24h.
- QA checklist:
  - Validate event_id uniqueness for 48h sample.
  - Confirm signature verification works against KMS public key.
  - Ensure matched_rule references a stable policy id and not a transient index.
  - Run end-to-end replay of 50 incidents through SIEM playbook and check alert fidelity.

Monitoring & KPIs:
- Key metrics to track (per-tenant and global):
  - export_eps_total, export_p95_latency_ms, export_queue_length, export_success_rate, parity_allow_deny_rate, avg_event_size_bytes.
- Pager thresholds:
  - export_success_rate < 98% for 10m -> P1 alert to SRE.
  - parity_allow_deny_rate < 99% for 30m -> P2 investigation with security lead.

Security & compliance considerations:
- All hosted exports must be signed and include provenance.
- For private deployments: document required configuration for signing or provide an unsigned mode that logs an explicit acceptance clause.
- Maintain an auditable migration log: every alias change, rule rename, and transform deployment must be recorded and exported to the governance bucket.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require signature verification for all customer-managed SIEM connectors? (Tradeoff: operational complexity vs forensic integrity).
- What is the maximum acceptable raw_payload retention for customers in regulated industries?
- Should transform code be maintained as a separate repository with semantic versioning or bundled into the exporter binary?

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Approve canonical schema and publish OpenAPI/JSON-Schema artifact (action: Priya, due: 2026-03-05).
- Build and publish transform libs (action: Ben, due: 2026-03-19).
- Kick off internal canary using test harness (action: Diego, due: 2026-03-12).

Appendix: sample canonical event (NDJSON single-line):
{"event_id":"evt-3f2b7e9a","timestamp_utc":"2026-02-27T18:12:04Z","recorded_at":"2026-02-27T18:12:04Z","actor":"user:ava.chen","actor_ip":"34.87.120.22","action":"resource.read","resource":"dataset/12345","resource_attrs": ["owner=team-ml","sensitivity=high"],"decision":"deny","decision_reason":"entitlement-missing","entitlement_paths": ["dataset.read","dataset.read.team-ml","dataset.read.team-ml.high-sensitivity"],"matched_rule":"policy-2026-01-09-03","resolved_attributes": ["region=us","env=prod"],"model_version":"rbac-engine@sha256:9f8a...","provenance":"hosted","signature":"BASE64SIG...","raw_payload":"H4sIAAAAA...BASE64"}
